subject.title: Feature: Handle Signal message edits (editMessage envelope)

question: When Signal receives an edit for a message that may already be in session context or driving an active run, should OpenClaw replace the original turn, append a structured correction, or cancel and re-dispatch the corrected content?
rationale: Signal transport parsing is straightforward, but transcript mutation and whether an edit wakes or cancels agent work define user-visible session semantics that cannot be selected safely from the issue alone.

options.title: Structured Correction
options.body: Record the edit against the target timestamp, supersede pending history when possible, and append a structured correction without rewriting persisted transcript history or automatically waking unmentioned group runs.

options.title: Replace Original Turn
options.body: Rewrite the original transcript entry and make subsequent context use only the corrected content, requiring a reliable persisted transcript mutation contract.

options.title: Cancel And Re-dispatch
options.body: Cancel active work for the target message and dispatch the edited content as a new instruction, aligning with the broader cross-channel behavior proposed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/55691.

recommendation.title: Structured Correction
recommendation.body: Record the edit against the target timestamp, supersede pending history when possible, and append a structured correction without rewriting persisted transcript history or automatically waking unmentioned group runs.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Signal receive and routing behavior most strongly traces to this feature history, including the owner boundary where the policy would first be applied.
